photoperiod.name: Photoperiod
photoperiod.description: Classic seeds, approx. 16 weeks. Flowering starts with the 12/12 light switch.

autoflower.name: Autoflower
autoflower.description: Automatic flowering, approx. 11 weeks. Light stays at 18 hours.

confirmations.startFlowering: Ready for flowering? From now on the light runs 12/12 – confirm to start the switch.
confirmations.harvest: Check the trichomes: milky with first amber tones? Then harvest and confirm – drying starts next.
confirmations.dryingDone: Do the branches snap instead of bending? Then drying is done – off to the curing jars.

seedling.1: Keep the medium slightly moist, never soaking wet – seedlings drown faster than they dry out.
seedling.2: High humidity (65–75 %) helps young roots; a propagator dome works great in the first days.
seedling.3: Keep the light dimmed (around 40 %) and at a good distance – bleached or curled leaves mean it’s too strong.
seedling.4: Don’t feed yet: the seed carries nutrients for the first two weeks.

germination.1: Seeds germinate dark and moist: between two damp paper towels or 1 cm deep straight into the medium, never standing in water.
germination.2: Around 24 °C round the clock is ideal – below 20 °C it takes days longer, above 28 °C the medium dries out.
germination.3: After 1–5 days the taproot breaks through. Once the sprout is above the soil it needs light: switch to “Seedling · with light”, or it stretches.
germination.4: No feeding and no pressing down: the seed brings what it needs for the first days.

vegetative.1: Water when the top few centimetres of the medium feel dry – lifting the pot tells you more than a schedule.
vegetative.2: Now is training time: topping or bending (LST) creates an even canopy and more bud sites.
vegetative.3: Raise light intensity step by step towards 80–100 % as the plants toughen up.
vegetative.4: Watch the VPD curve on Timeline: 0.8–1.1 kPa keeps transpiration and growth in balance.

flowering.1: Keep humidity at or below 50 % – dense buds plus high humidity is how mould starts.
flowering.2: Don’t change the light schedule anymore; interruptions of the dark period stress photoperiod plants.
flowering.3: Feed bloom nutrients and watch leaf colour – fading towards the end is normal.
flowering.4: Check the trichomes in the last weeks: cloudy with the first amber ones usually means harvest time.

drying.1: 16–20 °C and 55–60 % humidity, dark and with gentle air movement – slow drying preserves the terpenes.
drying.2: Plan for 10–14 days. If it’s done after 5, it was too warm or too dry.
drying.3: The snap test: when small branches crack instead of bending, the buds are ready for curing jars.
drying.4: Open the jars daily in the first curing week (“burping”) to let moisture escape.

vpd.title: VPD – vapour pressure deficit
vpd.text: How strongly the air draws water from the leaves, in kPa, worked out from humidity and leaf temperature (by default 2 °C below the air by day). It has no target of its own: it follows from the temperature and humidity targets. Low and high are those of single readings up to three days, and of means over five minutes beyond.

liveness.title: Online and stale
liveness.text: Online: the newest reading is less than 2 minutes old. Stale: less than 10. After that the device counts as offline, and its figures are dimmed rather than hidden – they are the last thing it measured.

band.title: On target
band.text: Close enough to the target to count as on it: within ±1 °C, ±5 % humidity or ±200 ppm CO₂. At night CO₂ has no band, because the device only adds CO₂ by day. After every switch between day and night the climate is given an hour to follow the new figures – on a fridge, plus the minutes its lamp and targets glide – and so it is for an hour after every change of the targets, the light plan or the operating mode. Meanwhile anything between the band before and the band after counts as on target, and the tile says “changing over”.

verdict.title: In band over 24 hours
verdict.text: The share of the last 24 hours in which temperature, humidity and, by day, CO₂ were all in their band – judged against the targets that applied at the time. Dips shorter than 10 minutes count, but are not named.

climatePreset.title: Climate preset
climatePreset.text: A ready climate for a phase: day and night temperature and humidity, the light hours, the light limit and CO₂. “Germination · dark” is a climate and an operating mode at once: dark, no CO₂, 24 °C and 75 % humidity for a humidifier round the clock; “Seedling · with light” is the first climate with light. Auto is for autoflowers, which keep 18–20 hours of light instead of going to 12/12.

stage.title: Phase
stage.text: The phase is where the plants are, from germination to curing. Germination means the same everywhere: seeds sprouting in the dark, and with its climate the device goes dark; seedling is the first phase with light. Entering one writes it on the grow: the date it began, a diary line, and its alarm rules on the devices the plants are with (curing has none). Only a germination recorded without its climate beside a device with its light on leaves that device’s alarms as they are. The phase counts the grow’s days and weeks – the feeding plan and the curves go by it. On a grow that is over, a phase added afterwards repairs what it went through and moves nothing else.

stepPreset.title: A preset in a step
stepPreset.text: Here a preset only names the phase more closely – “Auto” for an autoflower, “Late flower” for the last weeks. It sends no targets: the step writes the figures below and nothing else.

plan.title: Grow plan
plan.text: A list of steps, each with a phase, a length and the targets the device should hold. While it runs, the cloud moves on when a step’s time is up and sends the current step’s targets again every hour the device is online. Saving a plan does not start it, and at rest it writes nothing: the device keeps whatever it was last set to. A device whose settings have not arrived yet is sent no step – what a step carries would be put in place of its own tuning –, and one that states no climate has nowhere for the figures.

planMoves.title: Start and pause
planMoves.text: Start sends step 1’s targets to the device within half a minute, if it is online, and puts the grow here into the step’s phase if it names one – with its day counter and a diary line. Pause stops the step’s clock and sends nothing; the device keeps the targets it has until the plan runs again. To come in later, use “Continue the plan at a step” under the plan.

dayNight.title: Day and night
dayNight.text: The device takes day and night from the clock, not from whether the lamp shines: from “Light on at” it is day for the set length – the lamp ramps up to its light limit, the figures of the “Light on” column apply and CO₂ is dosed. Then it is night, with the figures of the “Light off” column. The column shaded green is the one in effect now. A light held by hand, a light limit of 0 % or a lamp dimmed by heat change none of that. Drying and germination have no day: they hold their figures round the clock, in the dark.

lightLimit.title: Light limit
lightLimit.text: The most the lamp may give by day, as a share of its full output: it ramps up to it at sunrise and down again at sunset. At 0 % it stays dark, but it is still day – with the day figures and with CO₂. Dark with no day at all are drying and germination · dark.

lightsOn.title: Light on at
lightsOn.text: When the light comes on and the day begins, on your account’s clock (Me › Account). When the clocks change for summer or winter time it stays at this time – the cloud resets the device itself on the night of the change, once your account’s time zone is set: the app picks it up at your first sign-in, and you can change it under Me › Account. For cheaper night power or a cooler summer tent, move the day into the night, from 22:00 for example. A running plan keeps this time unless its step brings one of its own.

resumePlan.title: Resume the plan
resumePlan.text: The plan’s clock runs on from where it stopped, and within the hour the step’s own figures are sent again, replacing those set here.

growDay.title: Grow day
growDay.text: Day 1 is the day the grow began. Every midnight adds one – counted on the calendar of whoever owns the grow.

growWeek.title: Week of the phase
growWeek.text: “Veg, week 2” is days 8 to 14 the grow has been in veg: a week of the phase counts from its own first day. How far the grow is overall is said by the day: day 1 is the day it began. In the diary a week is named by its days and carries the phase most of that week lay in.

autoTag.title: automatic
autoTag.text: This phase was set by a grow plan or a climate preset, which wrote the targets here along with it – it was not only recorded. It has nothing to do with autoflowers.

phasePreset.title: Targets with the phase
phasePreset.text: “Leave as they are” records only the phase: light, temperature and humidity stay as they are under Control. Choosing a climate switches the targets of the devices there right away – for Flower, for instance, the light goes to 12 hours, for “Germination · dark” the light goes off. That holds for every phase, germination and drying included: only recorded, it leaves the device as it is, and beside a device with its light on the alarms too. Out of germination or drying, only the climate of another phase brings the light back. Auto is for autoflowers, which keep long days. A new climate replaces the targets under Control; when the light comes on stays as it is. Drying holds the night figures round the clock, with no light and no CO₂. The alarms Too hot, Too cold and Too humid follow the phase; in germination Too humid rests unless you switch it on.

phaseCorrection.title: Correct or withdraw
phaseCorrection.text: Both change the record only: the phase’s date, the day count it starts and its diary line. Neither puts back the targets or the light the devices were given at the time.

autoflower.title: Photoperiod or autoflower
autoflower.text: A photoperiod plant flowers once the light goes to 12/12; an autoflower flowers by age and keeps long days. For autoflowers there is the Auto climate under Control and with every phase, and a feeding scheme chosen afterwards runs at half strength with no flip.

growEnds.title: Ending the grow
growEnds.text: Once the last plants are harvested the grow ends on this day: nothing can be dated after it, and it cannot be reopened in the app. Enter drying and curing first if they belong in the diary.

dayNightAverages.title: Day / night
dayNightAverages.text: Averages over the day and over the night: the hours the day figures applied and the hours the night figures applied. Where the device has no day and night – while drying, for one – a single average is shown.

feedStrength.title: Strength
feedStrength.text: Scales every dose in the scheme – half strength halves them. The EC targets stay as the scheme gives them.

waterEc.title: Water
waterEc.text: The EC of your water before anything is added. It is added to the scheme’s EC targets, so a target is what your meter should read; 0 means reverse osmosis water.

feedFlip.title: Flip week
feedFlip.text: The scheme is read by the grow’s own week, counted from day 1. The flip week says when the grow went to 12/12 and marks the scheme’s weeks from then on as flowering; it does not switch the light or enter a phase.

muteAll.title: Mute all
muteAll.text: For an hour nothing is sent to you, critical alarms included. What would have been sent in that hour is not sent later either – only a rule that repeats reports again afterwards, as long as its alarm is still open. Only you are muted: the others you share your places with are still told, and a rule with its own e-mail or webhook still sends.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.text: For working in the tent or cabinet: for a quarter of an hour the device stops the heater, the dehumidifier or compressor and the CO₂ valve, and dims the light; “Extend” adds another. Alarms stay off 10 minutes longer, until the climate is back. Then everything carries on by itself; you can also end maintenance sooner.

presetRules.title: Rules from the phase
presetRules.text: Each phase brings four rules – too hot, too humid, too cold at night and too much CO₂ – with lines worked out from the targets. The next phase moves their lines and waits; what you switched off, regraded or silenced stays, and curing removes them.

offlineRule.title: The offline rule
offlineRule.text: Every device has one rule that raises a critical alarm once nothing has been heard from it for ten minutes, plus the rule’s own wait. It cannot be deleted – only switched off, silenced or sent elsewhere.

alarmTemplates.title: Set up in one tap
alarmTemplates.text: One tap writes an ordinary alarm rule. For temperature and humidity its line comes from your targets: 5 °C over the warmer one, 4 °C under the cooler one, 10 points of humidity over the higher one and 20 under the lower one. “CO₂ cylinder empty” speaks up under 350 ppm, less than outdoor air: with a cylinder on the valve, it has run empty. “Fridge runs without a break” speaks up when the compressor runs 30 minutes without a pause – usually a door left open, a broken seal or too much heat from the lamp. Every one is critical, so it goes out by your notification settings, quiet hours included. Tap the rule to change its line, how long it waits or anything else.

alarmQuiet.title: Muting and maintenance
alarmQuiet.text: A muted rule keeps watching: the alert still shows under Alerts and marks the place on Home – it only tells nobody. Maintenance holds the alarms themselves back: for its 15 minutes and 10 more, while the climate comes back.

severity.title: Severity
severity.text: Critical and warning go out on the matching rows of each person’s notification settings, and only critical comes through quiet hours. Info is not announced there: it only shows under Alerts.

tellBy.title: Tell me by
tellBy.text: “My notification settings” reaches everyone who looks after this place, each by their own settings, mute and quiet hours. An e-mail address or a webhook reaches only that address, whatever anybody’s mute or quiet hours.

routingGrid.title: What goes where
routingGrid.text: Each row is a kind of message, each column a way to reach you; nothing is sent until you switch a cell on. A channel is off until it is configured, and its column cannot be switched until then; what is already routed to it is kept and starts carrying the moment the channel has somewhere to deliver to. The grid is yours alone – everyone you share places with sets their own – and an alarm rule with its own e-mail or webhook does not go through it.

emailAlarms.title: Alarms by e-mail
emailAlarms.text: Until a way is set up, nothing reaches you: no alarm, not even “device offline”, no task that is due and no camera that stopped delivering. One tap sends whatever may need you by e-mail to the address you sign in with: critical alarms if you have a device, warnings if you have a camera, due tasks if you keep a diary. Everything else stays as it is. Change or switch it off under Me › Notifications. “Later” hides this notice for a week.

quietHours.title: Quiet hours
quietHours.text: Between these times only critical alarms reach you. Warnings and the news that an alarm is over are not sent later; tasks and plan questions arrive once the quiet hours end.

rhythms.title: Rhythms
rhythms.text: A reminder is the rule: each time it falls due it shows above as a task, and ticking the task off moves the reminder on to its next date. The list above looks a week ahead.

rhythmEvery.title: Rhythm
rhythmEvery.text: “Every N days” counts from the last time it was ticked off, or from when it was set up – not from a calendar: ticking it early brings the next date forward, and missed dates do not pile up. “Once on” falls due at the start of that day.

taskFor.title: For
taskFor.text: For everyone: whoever owns the place or is a member of it is told when it falls due. For me: only you are.

socketRoles.title: Socket roles
socketRoles.text: Every smart socket is given a role at the device and switches with it: a heater socket with the heater, a light socket with the lamp, pump or timer by a cycle of its own, and a manual one only while you hold it. An exhaust runs from 0.8 °C over the target and stops just above it, a humidifier from 5 points of humidity under the target and stops at the target. The role is set when the socket is paired; it can be changed on the socket’s page under “Address, role, credentials”.

socketHold.title: Holding by hand
socketHold.text: On or Off holds the socket in that state for the time you choose, up to 24 hours; after that it switches by its role again. Auto ends it early, and so does a restart of the device. For another length, go to Auto first and choose again. A heater socket still stays off while the air is more than 5 °C above its target.

lightHold.title: Auto, on, off
lightHold.text: On keeps the lamp lit at its light limit, at night too; Off keeps it dark – for the time you choose or until the device restarts. Auto ends it early. Day and night stay where the light plan puts them: the same targets apply, and CO₂ is still dosed by day only. A socket with a light role follows the light output unless it is held itself. The device does not report a hold back: what is shown here is what this browser last sent, until its time is up.

firmwareChannel.title: Updates
firmwareChannel.text: Whether the device installs new firmware by itself. A newly added device has it switched on. On: new stable versions arrive on their own, with their fixes; the update channel below lets test versions (beta, alpha) in too. Off: it stays on the version it has until you install another one below. While an update installs, a controller or fridge module switches every output and socket off for a moment, then restarts.

stillCadence.title: A still every
stillCadence.text: How often the cloud asks this camera for a picture, 30 seconds at the least; after a failed try it waits twice as long each time, up to two hours. Older pictures are thinned: after a day one a minute is kept, after a week one every 5, after a month one every 15, after three months one an hour.

cameraPauses.title: Off in the dark, off during maintenance
cameraPauses.text: Off in the dark skips pictures while the device’s lamp is off – at night, but also at a light limit of 0 % or while drying; off during maintenance skips them while the device is in maintenance or switched off. Both only work for a camera that belongs to a device, and with off in the dark no warning is raised when this camera stops delivering.

staleWarning.title: Tells you
staleWarning.text: The warning comes once no picture has arrived for ten intervals, and ten minutes at the least – but not while its device is offline, which has an alert of its own. Logging failed captures writes a diary warning for every try that fails.

premiumCamera.title: Premium
premiumCamera.text: Premium belongs to one camera, not to the account, and never renews by itself: the offer is under Me › Premium on the camera’s card once its year is ending. A Terp Cam comes with 12 months when it is first paired; an RTSP camera has Premium only where it is bought for it. Without it, films are SD with a watermark, and HD and whole-grow films are not made. Self-hosted installations have no Premium, and nothing is locked there.

timelapses.title: Timelapses
timelapses.text: Films made from this camera’s stored pictures, 25 to the second. The day, week and month films rebuild themselves. The camera page plays the newest film of each kind; where there is none yet you make it: of the day chosen, the last complete week, the current phase or the whole grow.

overlays.title: Overlays
overlays.text: What is drawn on the film: the grow’s day, a temperature and humidity curve with the moment marked, and diary entries as captions. Each needs something to draw from – a grow, a device, entries – and is left out where there is none.

lightsOffFrames.title: Lights-off frames
lightsOffFrames.text: Left off, pictures taken while the device’s light was off are dropped, so the film does not flash dark every night. A picture with no light reading counts as lit.

render.title: Render
render.text: HD is 1920 pixels on the long side and needs Premium; SD is 1280, with a watermark unless the camera has Premium. Rendering the same days again with other settings replaces the film made before.

unpair.title: Unpair
unpair.text: The cloud stops reading this camera; its pictures and films stay. A Terp Cam stays paired to its device, though, and comes back here the next time the device reports it, for example after a restart.

rtsp.title: RTSP
rtsp.text: The live video stream most network cameras offer, at an address that starts with rtsp://. The cloud takes a still from it at the camera’s interval, as it does from a Terp Cam. Unlike a Terp Cam it comes with no year of Premium: Premium for it is bought, where the installation charges for it.

rolloutFailures.title: Failures that stop it
rolloutFailures.text: A device counts as failed once it was told to update and is not running the new build ten minutes later – offline devices included. At this many on a channel no further devices are told; the rollout carries on by itself once they report the build.

publicPage.title: Public page
publicPage.text: Anybody can read the diary at this address without an account – the phases, the days with their photos and the camera’s pictures. The address is made from the grow’s name, so it is not a secret; switching the page off takes it down at once.

linkActions.title: Change, revoke, forget
linkActions.text: Change sets a link’s days, pictures and expiry anew – wider as well as narrower – and keeps its address. Revoke stops the address working at once and keeps it in this list with the day it stopped. Forget appears once a link has stopped, revoked or run out, and takes it off the list. Neither can be undone.

shareWindow.title: From, to, expires
shareWindow.text: From and To decide which days of the diary the reader sees; left empty, they start at the beginning and keep up with the diary. Expires is the day the address itself stops working, at the end of that day in your time zone.

spaceLink.title: Grow or place
spaceLink.text: A link to a place shows its current climate against the targets – once its To date has passed, the climate of its last day instead – the grows there – private ones too – and its latest diary lines; a link to a grow shows that grow’s diary. Neither shows tasks or alerts.

privacyRedaction.title: Shared views
privacyRedaction.text: These hide figures from everyone who reads through a link, your public page or a follow. People you let into a place are not strangers: they still see weights and counts.

publicProfile.title: Public profile
publicProfile.text: Your profile page shows your username and your public grows. Switched off, the page is gone, but your username still shows on each public grow.

deleteAccount.title: Deleting the account
deleteAccount.text: Lines you wrote in other people’s places stay, without your name, and the climate readings stay with the devices, which can then be added again. A single grow is deleted from the grow’s own page.

passwordChange.title: Changing the password
passwordChange.text: Every other browser and app signed in as you is signed out; this one stays signed in.

memberRole.title: Roles
memberRole.text: “Can log” sees the place with its readings, grows and cameras, writes entries, adds photos and ticks off tasks. “Can manage” also changes targets, the plan, alarms, sockets and camera settings, and corrects other people’s entries. Devices, inviting and removing people stay with whoever manages the place. Read-only viewing is what share links do; there is no role for it.

invite.title: Inviting
invite.text: Anybody who has an invite link can join with it, as often as it is used, until it expires or you revoke it – revoking stops new joins, and whoever is in stays. Whoever joins needs an account of their own (e-mail, username and password) and sees the place – for a room, every place in it –, what is growing there, the cameras and every grow that was ever there, private ones too; not your other places, or grows that were never there. A username you already share a place with is added at once as “can log”, without being asked.

diaryLayer.title: Grow diary
diaryLayer.text: The diary is where you keep what you do to your plants – watering, feeding, photos, notes – and run grows with days and phases. While you do not use it, the app shows the climate and the device alone. It switches itself on once you start a grow or log something, and puts “Grow” and “Log” in the bar; under Me › Grow diary you can also switch it on or off by hand.

follow.title: Follow
follow.text: Keeps this grow under Me › Following for as long as it is public. The grower is not told who follows, and nothing is sent to you when it changes.

compressor.title: Compressor
compressor.text: In the fridge module one compressor both cools and dries: while it runs, temperature and humidity fall together. That is why it is listed under both readings – it is one machine, not two.

ppfd.title: PPFD
ppfd.text: How much of the light the plant can use reaches leaf level, in µmol per square metre and second. It is estimated from the sensor’s lux reading with the factor set for your device.

leafTemperature.title: Leaf temperature
leafTemperature.text: How warm the leaves themselves are, measured by the leaf sensor. Under the light they usually sit a little below the air, because they evaporate water – that is what the VPD is worked out from. There is no target of its own: the leaves follow the air and the light.

lux.title: Light intensity
lux.text: How bright it is at the light sensor, in lux. The curve shows when and how strongly the lamp shines. How much of it the plant can use is the PPFD, which is estimated from the lux.

climateControl.title: Control
climateControl.text: Switches the device’s whole climate control off and on again: heater, cooling or dehumidifying, light, CO₂ and fans, on the smart sockets too. While it is off the device keeps measuring and reporting, but holds no targets. Meant for an empty cabinet, for cleaning or for the time between two grows. It comes back on here, with any change to the light, the light limit, the targets or the climate preset under Control, or with the next plan step; a plan that switching off paused goes on once control is on. If the device is offline, that applies once it is back online.

energySaving.title: Energy saving
energySaving.text: With large plants and a lot of plant mass it can save energy not to run the back-wall fan all the time: it then rests while the compressor is off. Try it out. If the fridge then runs too long at a stretch, or the lamp dims because it gets too warm, switch the mode off again. As a rule of thumb, switch it on once the heater has to run constantly during the day.

operatingMode.title: Operating mode
operatingMode.text: What the device does as a whole while control is on. Standard holds temperature, humidity, light and CO₂ by day and night. Greenhouse holds the temperature only: light and CO₂ keep running by the light plan, the compressor only cools and does not dehumidify on purpose. Germination · dark and Drying are not chosen here: they belong to the phase and come and go with the climate preset under Control, with the climate of a phase of the grow or with a plan step. Energy saving applies to standard only.

cameraTunnel.title: Pull through the device
cameraTunnel.text: On, the cloud pulls the stream from your home network over the connection of the device in this place, so the camera needs no port forwarding and no dynamic DNS. Turn it off only for a camera reachable from the internet: the cloud then opens the stream itself, and the device’s connection is left alone.

cameraTransport.title: Transport
cameraTransport.text: How the stream is read. TCP is right for almost every camera. HTTP or HTTPS only where the camera offers RTSP tunnelled through HTTP alone. UDP only for a camera the cloud reaches directly; it does not pass through the device. Where no picture comes, try another setting and then “Take a picture now”.

updateChannel.title: Update channel
updateChannel.text: Which channel the device installs new firmware from by itself. Stable gets released versions only. Beta gets test versions before everyone else, alpha earlier ones still. Test versions can have faults a stable one does not.

firmwarePin.title: Firmware version
firmwarePin.text: With automatic updates off you choose the version yourself: any that was ever stable, or a newer one, for example to try a test version or to go back to an earlier stable one. While it installs, the device switches its outputs off for a moment and restarts. It stays on the version until you install another one or switch automatic updates back on.

co2Dosing.title: CO₂ dosing
co2Dosing.text: Throughout opens the valve whenever the reading drops below the switch-on point. In intervals, the Plantalytix Socket doses only in one window of every interval – for example 10 minutes every hour – so a fan can be slowed during that time.

co2Fan.title: Slow an AIR fan
co2Fan.text: While the Plantalytix Socket doses in intervals, an AIR fan runs at the set speed at most, so the CO₂ is not blown out again right away. The fan knows the Plantalytix Socket’s dosing windows for it; when its interval changes, the fan is told.

plugProtections.title: Protections
plugProtections.text: They switch the Plantalytix Socket off whatever it is controlling – above one temperature, below another – and keep minimum on and off times, so an appliance does not switch every few seconds. It comes back on only once the reading is back by the set gap.

lightRamp.title: Sunrise and sunset
lightRamp.text: How many minutes the light takes to come up in the morning and go down in the evening, 0 to 60. Fifteen minutes suits almost every lamp. 0 switches it hard – for drivers that flicker at low dimming levels.

maintenanceLight.title: Light on during maintenance
maintenanceLight.text: By day maintenance dims the light to 15 % anyway. Switched on, it also runs at 15 % during the dark period, so you can see what you are doing at night. In flower, light in the dark period disturbs the plants – leave it off then. A second light on a smart socket stays off during maintenance either way.

co2Night.title: CO₂ at night too
co2Night.text: Plants take up no CO₂ in the dark, so by default it is only dosed while the light is on. Roots in deep water culture (DWC) breathe round the clock, though – switch this on and the target is held at night as well. Maintenance pauses dosing either way.

fans.title: Fans
fans.text: The clip fan moves the leaves: seedlings do not like it at full strength, and at night the noise counts. 0 % stops it. The inner fans move the air around the cabinet; the figure is the least they run at, and they speed up when they need to. They do not go below 10 %.

compressorRest.title: Compressor rest
compressorRest.text: How long the compressor stays off at least before it may start again, which protects it from short-cycling. It cannot be less than 240 seconds; more makes the control slower, because cooling and dehumidifying have to wait longer.

leafOffset.title: Leaf against air
leafOffset.text: How much warmer or cooler than the air the leaf is taken to be wherever no leaf sensor measures it. That is what VPD is worked out with on Home, in the Timeline and with the targets. Under light a leaf evaporates water and is cooler: the default is −2 °C by day and 0 °C at night. Nothing is controlled by it.

ppfdFactor.title: Lux to PPFD factor
ppfdFactor.text: Turns the light sensor’s lux into PPFD. The right factor depends on the lamp’s spectrum: white full-spectrum LED about 0.015, high-pressure sodium (HPS) about 0.0122. With the wrong one the PPFD shown is up to 20 % off.

continuePlan.title: Continue the plan at a step
continuePlan.text: Puts the plan on a step of your choice: back to a step that ended too soon, or into the middle of a grow, straight into flower for instance. The step starts from the beginning, its values reach the device within a minute, and a grow in this place moves into its phase. A paused or stopped plan runs again afterwards.

co2Report.title: CO₂ cylinder
co2Report.text: When a cylinder goes in, note what it holds and – if you weighed it – what was left in the old one. From the valve ticks the device counts, the card works out how many ticks make a gram of CO₂. From the first empty cylinder on it estimates what is left in the one in use and how long it will last.

lightOverheat.title: Overheat protection
lightOverheat.text: Above this temperature at the light module the lamp dims itself down until it is cooler again. That protects the lamp and the plants right under it.

installApp.title: App on the home screen
installApp.text: Terp Control needs no app store: the browser puts the page on the home screen as an app with its own icon. It then opens full-screen without an address bar, and you stay signed in. On an iPhone it is also the only way to push notifications, because Safari delivers them only to apps on the home screen.

alarmRepeat.title: Repeat
alarmRepeat.text: While the alarm lasts, it is said again every so many minutes – for a warning or a notice just as for a critical alarm. That helps above all a webhook that switches something at home: if one call is lost, the next one comes. 0 says it once. An e-mail comes no more often than every five minutes.

webhookTemplate.title: Service for the webhook
webhookTemplate.text: For Home Assistant, Discord, Telegram and ntfy the app fills in the URL, method and messages from the few answers the service needs. What is saved is an ordinary webhook, which you can still change by hand. A Home Assistant address on the local network is called through the device’s tunnel automatically.

streamAddress.title: Stream address
streamAddress.text:
Where the camera offers its video stream, with its IP on your network (shown in your router or in the camera’s app). Common addresses:
Tapo: rtsp://IP:554/stream1
Reolink: rtsp://IP:554/h264Preview_01_main
Hikvision: rtsp://IP:554/Streaming/Channels/101
User and password go into the fields below. For Tapo that is the camera account from the Tapo app (Camera Settings › Advanced Settings › Camera Account), not your TP-Link account. A Reolink camera needs RTSP switched on in its network settings.
Where a device is in the place the camera looks at, the cloud pulls the stream from your network through it. Otherwise it opens the stream itself, and the address has to be reachable from the internet.

stepLightHours.title: Light on for (in a step)
stepLightHours.text: How many hours a day the light is on while this step runs. It comes on at the usual time (“Light on at” under Targets) – unless the step brings a time of its own – and goes off that many hours later; the night is the rest of the day. Twelve hours is what makes photoperiod plants flower. Left empty, the light keeps the hours it has.

readyPlans.title: Ready-made plans
readyPlans.text: Two whole grows for the fridge: photoperiod (about 16 weeks, flower starts with the switch to 12 hours of light) and autoflower (about 11 weeks, the light stays at 18 hours). Every step brings its phase’s targets; before flower, before harvest and at the end of drying the plan waits for you. Choosing one opens the plan to look through; nothing is written until “Save plan”.

drying.title: Drying
drying.text: While drying the device knows no day and no night: the light stays off, no CO₂ is dosed, it only dehumidifies and heats to the drying targets. Drying starts with the “Drying” preset under Control, as the climate of the drying phase in the grow or with a drying plan step. Another preset – the climate of a phase included – or a plan step end it with targets of their own. Entering a phase without its climate, or withdrawing one, changes nothing on the device: it goes on drying until drying is ended under Control. “Control off” brings back the targets from before drying, and the device goes back to its operating mode, energy saving included.

germination.title: Germination · dark
germination.text: Seeds germinate in the dark: the device goes into its germination mode – no light, no CO₂, only a humidifier holding the humidity – and heats and cools to one temperature round the clock. In a tent the exhaust does the cooling; a dehumidifier stays off, as it would warm the tent and dry out the medium the seeds sprout in. 24 °C is suggested, the middle of the 22–26 °C seeds sprout fastest at. Germination also brings 75 % humidity: seeds sprout well between about 70 and 90 % – drier, the medium dries out on top and the seed coat hardens; wetter, water stands on the medium and the tray. 75 % sits safely in between, below the 90 % at which “Too humid” warns, and the seedling after it holds 65–70 %. Only a humidifier on a smart socket can hold it; once germination ends, the humidity from before applies again. Germination starts with “Germination · dark” under Control, as the climate of the germination phase, during setup or with a germination plan step. Any other climate – the climate of a phase included – or plan step – one without a phase too – ends it: the device holds day and night with light again, on standard with its energy saving. Entering a phase without its climate, or withdrawing one, changes nothing on the device, its alarms included: it goes on germinating until germination is ended under Control. Whether “Too humid” warns during germination and whether a humidifier holds the humidity is chosen wherever germination is set; while it runs, both are changed under Control in the climate preset.

germinationAlarm.title: “Too humid” during germination
germinationAlarm.text: Germinating seeds are kept moist on purpose, and a germination box often reads far above what is good for leaves. So the phase’s “Too humid” rests during germination unless you switch warning on – an alarm that goes off every night is soon ignored. Switched on, it warns above 90 % during germination, whether you set germination under Control, with a phase or with a plan (above that, water stands on the medium and the tray, where mould and damping-off begin); a device that has none gets one. After germination its own line applies again. Alarms you set up yourself, and every other alarm, always stay awake. Resting means the alarm stays switched on and keeps your settings; an open alert ends without an all-clear and is listed under Alerts as “resting during germination”. The choice is for this germination; the next one starts without warning again.

germinationHumidifier.title: Humidifier during germination
germinationHumidifier.text: During germination the device controls the temperature alone. A humidifier on a smart socket still holds germination’s humidity, 75 % unless you set another: it switches on once the air is at least 5 points drier and off as soon as the figure is reached – it never makes it wetter than set. So the air never falls below 70 %, the low end of what seeds sprout well in, and stays well below the 90 % at which “Too humid” warns. Holding is the default, because dry air fails a germination sooner than humid air does: the medium dries out. Switched off, the humidifier rests until germination ends – one that is running switches off straight away – and works as before afterwards. While it holds the humidity, you set it for germination under Control. The choice is for this germination; the next one starts with the humidity held again.

socketTimer.title: Timer
socketTimer.text: A socket with the role Pump or Own timer switches by its own cycle, not by the climate: for example on for 2 minutes, every 6 hours. Without a timer it stays off. The cycle keeps running on the device even when the connection to the cloud is gone.

plugMode.title: Switches by
plugMode.text: What the Plantalytix Socket controls with its own sensor: heating, cooling, humidifying, dehumidifying or CO₂ – then it switches at two points of the reading. With a timer it switches at set times of day, and Off keeps it off. CO₂ needs the CO₂ sensor sold as an accessory; without it the Plantalytix Socket stays off. Dosing in intervals and slowing an AIR down are on the Plantalytix Socket’s page under Advanced.

plugDayNight.title: Day and night
plugDayNight.text: The Plantalytix Socket knows the day only as a time: it begins at “Day from” and ends at “Night from”, on your clock. With switch points of their own at night it holds other values at night; in CO₂ mode it does not dose at night at all.

switchPoints.title: Switch points
switchPoints.text: Two values rather than one target: at one the Plantalytix Socket switches on, at the other off. The gap between them keeps it from switching back and forth with every reading – the wider it is, the less often it switches, and the further the reading swings.

timerWindows.title: Time windows
timerWindows.text: When the Plantalytix Socket is on, the same every day: from a time of day for so many minutes. A window may run past midnight. The times are on your clock and move with daylight saving time.

fanMode.title: Fan mode
fanMode.text: Fixed: the AIR runs at one set speed by day and another at night. By temperature, humidity or both: it runs at its lowest speed while the reading stays under the target, and speeds up the further the reading rises above it – up to its highest speed. Day, for the AIR, is while its light sensor sees light. By temperature it speeds up from 1 °C below the target and runs at its highest speed 1 °C above it, by humidity from 5 % below to 5 % above. By both it follows whichever reading is further over its target.

fanSpeeds.title: Speed
fanSpeeds.text: As a share of full speed. In fixed mode one value applies by day and one at night. Controlled, the fan never runs slower than “At least” and never faster than “Most” – so the night stays quiet and the air still moves.

nightBand.title: Band, night and spread
nightBand.text: The green band is the target range, at night the night figures’ one. The grey stretches are the nights: the hours the light plan makes night – the light off, the night figures applying, no CO₂ dosed. The pale area around a curve reaches from the lowest to the highest reading of each point: a door that stood open for 40 seconds still shows in a day’s picture. For VPD over more than three days those are means over five minutes. The strips under a curve show when an output ran – the stronger, the longer within that stretch. For the hour after each switch – on a fridge, from the start of its dimming – and after every change of the targets, the light plan or the operating mode the band spans the figures from before and after: that is how long the climate is given to follow. Where nothing alternates – drying, germination, 24 or 0 h of light – nothing is grey, and the band is the one target that applies round the clock.

dayShare.title: On target
dayShare.text: The part of the day temperature and humidity were on target: within ±1 °C and ±5 %.

mixing.title: Mixing
mixing.text: Add them to the water in this order and set the pH last. The scheme’s figures are a guide, not a rule.

feedGrid.title: The grid
feedGrid.text: Tap a cell to change it; a row is a product, and “+ Product” adds one of your own. The flower columns begin in the week of the flip. EC figures are what your meter should read with this water (chart value + water EC). The manufacturer’s chart is a starting point, not a rule. Changes to this grid only affect what these plants get. A scheme on your own shelf is a copy: edited later, every running grow stays fed exactly as before.

harvestWeights.title: Weight
harvestWeights.text: The dry weight only comes days later: both fields may stay empty and be filled in on the plant afterwards. A plant that really weighed something else is corrected on the plant itself.

socketAddress.title: Pairing by IP
socketAddress.text: This pairs a Tasmota socket – NOUS, Athom or a Shelly you flashed yourself – on the same Wi-Fi as the device, by its IP address or its name on the local network. Switching happens on the local network, from the device: the socket only has to be reachable for the device, not from the internet. User and password are only needed if the socket has a web password; when a socket is changed, empty fields keep what it has. A Terp Control socket is paired on the device itself: press the button, then Smart Sockets.

deviceName.title: Name
deviceName.text: What the device is called in the app. Leave it empty and the device is called after its type – and, where you have more than one of them, after the last characters of its id, the ones printed on it.

deviceMove.title: Moving
deviceMove.text: From the move on, the device’s readings count for the new place; what it measured so far stays with the old one. The camera that runs through the device, its sockets and its alarms move with it. A grow does not: you move that on the grow’s page. A new place is made in the room the device is in now.

alarmFor.title: For how long
alarmFor.text: How long the reading has to stay past the line before the alarm is raised; 0 raises it at once. For an output watched for running at all: how long it has to run without a pause before that is an alarm rather than a cycle. For “Device offline” the time comes on top of the ten minutes after which a device counts as offline.

streamChange.title: Changing the address
streamChange.text: The password the stream is opened with stays with the server and is never sent back here. When you change the address, user and password stay as they are if you leave them empty. Pictures, films and Premium stay with this camera. After saving, “Take a picture now” checks that it is reachable.

claimCode.title: The code
claimCode.text: The device shows a short code on its display, and the box carries the same one as a QR code. It is the whole proof that you have the device in front of you.

claimLater.title: It can wait
claimLater.text: The device works without a camera too. One can be paired later with the devices under Control, where the presets are changed as well; notifications are under Me.

accountExport.title: Export everything
accountExport.text: Every grow, your diary photos and the finished films in one zip: JSON, CSV and the pictures. The climate comes as a row a minute, averaged, rather than as the reading every few seconds it was measured at. Single camera stills stay in the app – there are tens of thousands of them – and the zip counts them per camera.

publicGrow.title: Public grows
publicGrow.text: A public grow shows a stranger the diary from its first day: the phases, the days with their photos and the camera’s pictures, the climate averages, the strains, and your handle. Harvest weights and plant counts follow your privacy settings. It never shows the place’s current readings, its devices, its alarms or its tasks, and never your e-mail. Followers see the same page, and nobody can write.

timezone.title: Time zone
timezone.text: The time zone is kept with your account. Every clock time the app draws and the quiet hours are read in it – the same on every device, wherever it is.

sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.text: Every browser and script signed in as you. A session that was ended has to sign in again.

tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.text: Your reminders and the grow-plan steps waiting for you. What you tick off here is written to the diary too.

firmwareClasses.title: Device classes
firmwareClasses.text: A channel points at a build, and every device of the class that follows that channel is told to install it. Nothing here is written until Apply, and what the change would reach is shown under the controls.

firmwareRegister.title: Register a build
firmwareRegister.text: A build is registered before it has any bytes; its files are uploaded against it afterwards. The version is the uuid the build container stamped it with, and is never compared with another.

demoObjects.title: What the demo shows
demoObjects.text: What a demo visitor sees: every place, device, camera and grow marked as a demo object. Nothing on this screen writes – the mark is a property of the database with no route behind it, and is set where the demo is seeded.

adminAddresses.title: Addresses
adminAddresses.text: An address is on this screen and on no other in the app. The search reads only what is already loaded, so nothing typed here is sent anywhere.

rolloutStages.title: Firmware rollout
rolloutStages.text: A class hands its build out on stable, beta and alpha. A stage tells a share of the class at a time, and the share is taken from each device’s id, so a device inside it stays inside it as it grows. A device reports the build it is running within minutes of installing it.

removeMember.title: Taking somebody out
removeMember.text: What somebody wrote here stays in the diary and goes on carrying their name. Whoever came in on a link takes that link with them: anybody else you sent that one to can no longer join. Whoever is already in stays in, your other links are untouched, and a new link is one tap away. Somebody who was also let into the room keeps its places.

stepSettings.title: What a step writes
stepSettings.text: A step writes the figures it is given into the device’s settings: the day and night targets, the CO₂ target, the light’s limit and how long it is on. A figure left empty stays what the device has, and so does everything else in its settings. Where the device reports no CO₂ sensor, no CO₂ target is written – its firmware holds one at zero whatever it is told. A step into drying or germination switches the device dark and writes only what it holds there; the next step brings the light back, one without a phase too – unless it is a germination itself. Where a device has not sent its settings yet, the plan sends it no step: what the step carries would be put in place of the device’s own tuning, and every setting it does not name would be back at a factory value.

lightHardStart.title: Without ramping up
lightHardStart.text: The device counts its day not from your midnight but from a fixed hour, earlier or later than yours depending on the time zone and summer time. A light window that runs past that hour switches the light on in the morning without ramping up; in the evening it dims down as usual. A window that lies within one of the device’s days ramps up in the morning too.
